title: The True Nature of Women: Emotional Creatures, Deceivers & Charmers of Men
summary: First part of the third arc of his 'Educated Barbarian' Nietzsche series, on Nietzsche's view of women. He argues women evolved as masters of emotion, charm and concealment, that modern feminism and disenchantment (science, porn, hypersexualization) stripped them of this soft power, and that the traditional arrangement gave women more real power and safety than modern independence does.
claims: He presents Nietzsche, often branded sexist by mainstream media, as an early 'ancient feminist' once you actually read the books
Being physically weaker, women evolved to specialise in emotion: reading, using and evoking feelings in others as a survival strategy
Calling women emotional is only sexist if you assume emotional intelligence is inferior to logic and memory, which IQ tests mostly measure; he sees emotion as their strength
Manipulation is the strength of the weak, the way poison is the weapon of those who lack physical force
Men want affection more than sex; knowing someone is waiting for you and loves you is central to a man's life, first filled by the mother and later by a spouse
Men who resent women's emotional pull feel enslaved because they give but get nothing tangible back; the exchange has shifted
Per Nietzsche, a woman learns to hate in proportion as she forgets how to charm; one consumed by hate loses the ability to charm, mostly to her own detriment
Women are ambivalent and can use their power for good or harm, so a man must choose a woman who uses it well, just as a woman should choose a man who protects rather than hurts
In an argument a woman who is losing will drag it into emotion, where she wins; a man should stay logical rather than follow her there
A healthy relationship is a constant back-and-forth like a rough sea; if your woman stops fighting, she has given up on you
A woman appeals to a man just by existing; a man must perform to appeal to a woman
Don't resent your appetite for women or become a simp; be an 'enlightened slave' who gives only what is reasonable and keeps independence and self-control
He explains hostility from gay men toward women and lesbians toward men as seeing the other sex without the veil of lust
The romantic veil of projection between the sexes keeps heterosexual relationships and reproduction going; modern science, porn and red-pill content have torn it
Porn disenchants women: men have seen everything before discovering a real woman, so the mystery is gone
Modern 'hyper-male' masculinity gurus and 'hyper-female' women are caricatures that reveal too much rather than real masculinity or femininity
Mystery is half of a woman's charm; the most exciting part of dating is the chase, when she is still unknown
Women in male-dominated workplaces either keep their femininity and bring sexual tension, or masculinise themselves; high-ranking women are typically very disagreeable
Nietzsche calls man the 'barren animal'; barrenness leads to a more virile, severe taste in life, and biology will not change
Exceptionally gifted women should be free to pursue careers instead of motherhood, but for most women giving life is the most important thing they will do
He defines modern feminism as making women do what men do and calling it freedom, though men were never free either
Men are built to grind in labour; women pushed into office work become miserable, being too emancipated rather than not enough
A documentary of a woman living as a man for a year: she concluded life as a woman is better because society protects and supports women
Women want a man's freedom without the responsibility; freedom for a man is a free fall with no safety net
In his family the grandfather is the official patriarch, but his grandmother really ran things through her hold on his heart
Per Nietzsche, in revenge and in love woman is more barbarous than man; the world of emotion controls the world of action
He argues a woman 100 years ago was happier than today: less freedom but more safety and security
Allowing women to leave bad relationships was a good safeguard, but modern women threw out relationships entirely (baby with the bathwater)
A thought experiment: the sex that works, takes risks and dies in wars is the oppressed one, while the one supported at home is privileged
Women chose soft power over hard power, which is why far fewer women are assassinated or killed in battle
Young, attractive, fertile women are the most privileged people on earth; the world bends around them
A woman's beauty-based power is time-limited; a smart woman uses it while young to secure a man's commitment and protection
He predicts that within 10-15 years there will be a wave of suicides among childless women in their 30s and 40s
Women are 'witches' who bend reality through emotion; trading the wand for a knife (action) makes them less effective
This Nietzsche-on-women arc is planned to run six parts, with the follow-up two weeks later
